title: Synthesis, cholinesterase inhibition, antiproliferative activity, and  in silico  evaluation of novel hydantoin conjugates
content: A new series of novel hydantoin conjugates 3a–q was synthesized using a facile route and obtained in excellent yields. The newly synthesized conjugates were characterized using FTIR, 1H-NMR, 13C-NMR, and HRMS analyses, and their cholinesterase [acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and butyrylcholinesterase (BChE)] inhibitory and antiproliferative properties were subsequently evaluated. Among the tested compounds, 3d and 3p were identified as potent BChE inhibitors (IC50 = 10 ± 1.43 and 18 ± 2.65 µM). To explore antiproliferative activity, all the compounds were screened against MCF7, A549, and PC3 cancer cell lines. Compound 3j displayed the most potent antiproliferative effect (IC50 = 13.95, 16.53, and 34.62 µM, respectively) against MCF7, A549, and PC3 cancer cell lines, while 3d, 3h, 3k, and 3q also exhibited considerable cytotoxicity. Notably, the most active compounds exhibited low toxicity to normal HDF cells (IC50 = 117–429 µM), indicating a favorable selectivity towards cancer cells. An in silico molecular docking study of compounds against AChE and BChE, respectively, suggested the involvement of key amino acid residues in ligand–enzyme interactions. Thus, 3j emerges as a promising cytotoxic candidate, while 3d and 3p represent promising BChE inhibitors, paving the way for further optimization and mechanistic investigation.
